question: White AgCl turns grey in presence of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**sunlight.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When **silver chloride** (AgCl) is exposed to** sunlight, **it undergoes** photodecomposition **and forms silver metal and chlorine gas.
 
• This reaction causes the white AgCl to turn** grey.**
 
• AgCl is a **white, insoluble, and inert** compound that is commonly used in photography and silver plating.
 
• It is also used in the production of specialty **glass, ceramics, and catalysts.**
 
• CO₂ and O₂ **do not** have any significant effect on AgCl.
 
• Water can cause AgCl to dissolve and form a **colorless solution**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **CO₂** is a **colorless and odorless **gas that is present in the atmosphere.

 
 
• It is a** greenhouse gas **that contributes to global warming.
 
• It is also used in the production of** carbonated beverages, dry ice, and fire extinguishers.**
 
 
 
• **O₂** is a **colorless and odorless **gas that is essential for the survival of most living organisms.
 
 
• It is used in the production of **steel, welding, and medical applications.**
 
 
 
• **Sunlight** is a form of **electromagnetic radiation** that is emitted by the sun.
 
 
• It contains a range of wavelengths, including** ultraviolet (UV) radiation**.
 
• UV radiation can cause **photodecomposition** of certain compounds, such as AgCl.
